prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The five frames show an outdoor open-ground scene with one nearby person generally in front of the camera wearer, parts of the wearer’s arms/hands and a dark bag close to the lens, and cars farther behind or to the side. The bright foreground regions place the wearer’s hand and bag within roughly 0.2–0.8 m, while the standing person appears about 0.8–2 m away; the visible cars are approximately 3–10 m away, with the landscape extending beyond them. Across the strip, the person shifts from partly left/out of view to centered and close, then remains near the center-right as the camera turns or moves closer; the bag and hands repeatedly occlude the lower foreground. The depth map makes near-versus-far layering and occlusion boundaries clearer than RGB, but it is unreliable at frame seams, thin limbs and fingers, object edges, and on the person’s dark clothing, and its monocular brightness does not support precise metric distances or dependable distances between separated objects.
descriptions.segmentation: The masks identify several person regions, a nearby motorcycle-like region in the second frame, a small cellphone near the central person’s hand in the third frame, and distant truck/car regions in the third and fourth frames. The main person is in front of the wearer at roughly 1–2 m, while the labeled vehicles are behind that person or off to the side at roughly 4–10 m; foreground arms, hands, and the bag lie within arm’s reach but are inconsistently classified, with some regions mislabeled as people. Over time, the main person grows from partially visible on the left to a large central or right-side mask, indicating approach and/or camera turning, while vehicles remain small and distant; the person faces broadly toward the camera in the later frames, though head and gaze direction are not resolved. Segmentation clarifies instance extents, overlaps, and which small regions may be separate objects, but several labels and boundaries are unreliable: the bag/arms receive implausible person or motorcycle masks, distant objects are fragmentary, and large portions of bodies and objects are cut off by image borders or occluded.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only hands: a hand low-left in the first frame, a near-vertical hand around center-left in the second, and an extended hand near the center in the third; no dependable body skeleton appears in any frame, and the last two frames are blank. These detections place the hands in front of the camera wearer, with the third-frame hand extending laterally from the nearby person or foreground interaction region and overlapping the space above the bag; relative to RGB, they are likely within roughly 0.3–1.2 m of the camera, but exact ownership and distance are uncertain. The hand configurations change from low and partly cropped, to upright, to horizontally extended, after which they become occluded, leave the field of view, or fail detection as the camera faces the nearby person more directly. The map makes finger and hand orientation easier to see than RGB, but it cannot establish whole-body position, facing direction, gaze, or reach for either person, and the missing body pose plus sparse, sometimes incomplete keypoints make it highly unreliable outside the three detected hands.
